sentences.text: The genus Bellubrunnus contains only one known species, Bellubrunnus rothgaengeri.
This pterosaur is distinguished by lacking long tail vertebrae projections, having fewer jaw teeth, and possessing wingtips that curve forward instead of backward.
The holotype represents one of the smallest known pterosaur fossils, with a wingspan of less than one foot.
Twenty-one small teeth are preserved in the holotype specimen.
The eyes are exceptionally large, occupying about one-third of the skull's total length.
The humerus is exceptionally long compared to the femur, with a length ratio of 1.4, a unique trait distinguishing it from other rhamphorhynchids.
The femur lacks a neck between the head and shaft, a unique characteristic of Bellubrunnus.
The genus Bellubrunnus was first described and named in 2012 by David W. E. Hone, Helmut Tischlinger, Eberhard Frey, and Martin Röper.
The holotype specimen was discovered in the summer of 2002 by a team led by Monika Rothgaenger, after whom the species is named.
The only known specimen of Bellubrunnus is a single complete and articulated skeleton cataloged as BSP–1993–XVIII–2.
The fossil was found in a quarry at Kohlstatt near Brunn, in rock layers beneath the Solnhofen Limestone.
Features such as a shortened skull, large eyes, unfused skull bones, and poorly ossified limbs suggest the specimen was an immature individual when it died.
Short chevrons and zygapophyses on the tail vertebrae indicate that Bellubrunnus had a relatively flexible tail.
The forward-curving wingtips may have improved maneuverability by increasing air resistance and turbulence, though their exact function remains unknown.
The curved wingtips may have helped stabilize the wing membrane flaps, which were prone to fluttering in other pterosaurs.
It is hypothesized that Bellubrunnus was a fish-eater and possibly the direct evolutionary ancestor of Rhamphorhynchus, though this relationship requires more fossil evidence to confirm.
Bellubrunnus is classified within the family Rhamphorhynchidae and the subfamily Rhamphorhynchinae.
Bellubrunnus lived during the Late Jurassic (Kimmeridgian stage) in southern Germany.
The fossil dates to approximately 151 million years ago, during the late Kimmeridgian stage of the Late Jurassic.
The Brunn limestones, where Bellubrunnus was found, were likely deposited in lagoons and reefs of an island region.

O'Sullivan and Martill (2015) argued that many distinguishing features of Bellubrunnus are problematic due to a lack of ontogenetic studies, leaving it uncertain whether it is a distinct genus or merely a juvenile form of Rhamphorhynchus.

Despite similarities, O'Sullivan and Martill noted that the lack of elongate tail supports and the forward-curving fourth wing phalanx suggest Bellubrunnus may not be the same species as Rhamphorhynchus muensteri.
